title: Rule out the shapes this could be, but isn't
explanation: `top` shows event-shipper at ~0% CPU -- not a busy loop. `ps aux | grep event-shipper` shows a normal, live process, not `<defunct>` -- not a zombie either. It's genuinely alive and genuinely idle, which is its own distinct failure mode: `ps`/`top` alone can't tell "stuck forever" apart from "idling as designed" (e.g. a legitimate `sleep infinity`).

title: Ask the kernel exactly what it's parked inside
explanation: Get its PID (`cat /var/run/telemetry/event-shipper.pid`), then `cat /proc/<pid>/status | grep State` (interruptible sleep, `S`) and, more precisely, `cat /proc/<pid>/wchan` -- the specific kernel function it's blocked in. It reads `wait_for_partner`, the kernel's name for a process blocked opening one end of a named pipe (FIFO) while nothing has opened the other end.

title: This is expected pipe semantics, not a bug in event-shipper
explanation: event-shipper's own source opens `/run/app.pipe` for writing (`exec 3>/run/app.pipe`) as its very first action. Opening a FIFO write-only is defined to block in the kernel until some other process opens it for reading -- so the question isn't "what's wrong with event-shipper", it's "what's supposed to be reading from this pipe, and is it running?"

title: Trace the missing reader to a dropped config entry
explanation: `log-collector` is the intended reader, started by the same control script (`/usr/local/bin/svc-ctl`) that reads its service list from `/etc/telemetry/services.conf`. That file only lists `SERVICES="event-shipper"` -- an edit dropped `log-collector`, so it never starts, and the pipe's read end never opens.

title: Fix the other side of the handshake, not the stuck process
explanation: Add `log-collector` back to the config and start it directly (`sudo svc-ctl start log-collector`). event-shipper itself needs no restart at all: the instant a reader opens the pipe, its already-blocked `open()` call returns immediately and it resumes writing on its own.

title: Verify the block actually cleared, not just that a new process exists
explanation: `cat /proc/<event-shipper-pid>/wchan` should now show something like `hrtimer_nanosleep` -- back in its normal `sleep 2` cycle instead of `wait_for_partner` -- and `/var/log/telemetry/events.log` should be visibly growing, proving events are flowing end-to-end rather than just that a reader process is technically running.
